description: A rectangle with a narrow bay, 2 feet square, pushed out of its south side: the south eave is two collinear edges, 0 and 4, either side of the bay, facing the same way. Once the bay's little hip closes, their faces meet, in one plane: the boundary between them, from the valleys' meeting point to the main ridge, is a seam and not a line, and each face is still its own edge's.
